Root Condition.

The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root.
Dependent on a tainted wholesome state, a tainted wholesome state arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state free from taints (*anāsava*), a wholesome state free from taints arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated.

3.4.2.1.7. Chapter on Questions (Pañhāvāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka) – Root Condition (Hetu)
A conditioned wholesome state accompanied by taints (*sāsava*) is a condition, by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*), for a conditioned wholesome state accompanied by taints.

A wholesome state not accompanied by taints (*anāsava*) is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a wholesome state not accompanied by taints. (Abbreviated. There are two [conditions] in the case of the root;

two in the case of the object (*ārammaṇa*); three in the case of the predominance (*adhipati*); two in the case of the immediate (*anantara*) …pe… two in the case of the support (*nissaya*); four in the case of the decisive support (*upanissaya*); two in the case of the repetition (*āsevana*) …pe… two in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*). (Abbreviated.)
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods were calculated for the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so too should they be calculated here. 3.4.2.2.
Unwholesome Section: Root Condition (*Hetu*)
Dependent on a state that is with taints and unwholesome, a state that is with taints and unwholesome arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.

The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka)
Dependent on a conditioned, indeterminate state accompanied by taints, a conditioned, indeterminate state accompanied by taints arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a conditioned, indeterminate state free from taints, a conditioned, indeterminate state free from taints arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is both untainted (*anāsava*) and indeterminate (*abyākata*), a state that is tainted (*sāsava*) and indeterminate arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is both untainted and indeterminate, states that are both tainted and indeterminate arise by way of the root condition.

Dependent on a state that is both with-taints and indeterminate, and a state that is without-taints and indeterminate, there arises a state that is with-taints and indeterminate by way of root-condition.

The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root.

The Tetrad of Conditions— Root Condition (Hetu)

Root Condition Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with the taints, an unwholesome state associated with the taints arises by way of the root condition … three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state dissociated from the taints (*āsava*), an unwholesome state associated with the taints arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on both an unwholesome state associated with the taints and an unwholesome state dissociated from the taints, an unwholesome state associated with the taints arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are five [types of conditions] for the root; five for the object (*ārammaṇa*) ... pe ... five for non-disappearance (*avigata*).

Three; with associated [condition], five …pe… with non-disappearance [condition], five. (Abbreviated.

3.4.3.3. The Indeterminate Section (*Abyākata-pada*).
Root Condition:
Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints (*āsava*) and indeterminate (*abyākata*), there arises a state dissociated from the taints and indeterminate by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root condition there is one; under object condition there is one ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there is one. (Abbreviated.)
One [condition] by way of not-root; one by way of not-object; one by way of not-predominance …pe… one by way of not-disappearance. (Abbreviated.

Root.

The Tetrad of Conditions—Root (Hetu)

Dependent on a state that is both an *āsava* and associated with an *āsava* (*sāsava*), and unwholesome, there arises a state that is both an *āsava* and associated with an *āsava*, and unwholesome, by way of root condition... three.

Dependent on a state that is associated with an *āsava* but is not itself an *āsava*, and unwholesome, there arises a state that is associated with an *āsava* but is not itself an *āsava*, and unwholesome, by way of root condition... three.

Dependent on a state that is both an *āsava* and associated with an *āsava*, and unwholesome, and a state that is associated with an *āsava* but is not itself an *āsava*, and unwholesome, there arises a state that is both an *āsava* and associated with an *āsava*, and unwholesome, by way of root condition... three. (Abbreviated.)
In the cause condition, nine; in the object condition, nine … pe … in the non-disappearance condition, nine. (Abbreviated.

Not-root.

(Abbreviated. The Tetrad of Conditions—Root Condition (Hetu)

An unwholesome state that is both an *āsava* and associated with an *āsava* is a condition, by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*), for an unwholesome state that is both an *āsava* and associated with an *āsava*. (Abbreviated. [In the Positive Enumeration:

seven for root, nine for object, nine for predominance …pe… nine for decisive support and repetition, three for kamma, nutriment, faculty, and jhāna, nine for path, association …pe… nine for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.

it is a condition by way of conascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*); it is a condition by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*). (Abbreviated. [In the negative analysis:
nine [conditions] excluding root; nine excluding object. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, not-object: seven. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object: nine. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive enumerations were calculated for the Question Section of the Wholesome Triplet, so should they be calculated here.)

Under root-condition: one; under object-condition: one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition: one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence ... pe ... and in the section on inquiry, it is likewise one in all cases.

The "Treatise on the Couplets of the Taints and Things Subject to Taints" and the "Treatise on the Triads of the Wholesome" are concluded. 3.4.5. The Couplets on the Taints and Things Associated with the Taints; the Triads on the Wholesome.
3.4.5.1. Section on the Wholesome (Kusalapada) 3.4.5.1.1–6: The Chapter on Dependence, etc. (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka)

Dependent on a root-cause (hetu) that is both an outflow (āsava) and associated with an outflow—an unwholesome state—an outflow that is both an outflow and associated with an outflow arises by way of the root-cause condition ... three.

Dependent on an unwholesome state that is associated with an outflow but is not itself an outflow, an unwholesome state that is associated with an outflow but is not itself an outflow arises by way of the root-cause condition ... three.
Dependent on a state that is both an *āsava* and associated with an *āsava*, and also unwholesome;

and dependent on a state that is both associated with an *āsava* and unwholesome, but is not itself an *āsava*, an *āsava* that is both associated with an *āsava* and unwholesome arises by way of the root condition.
… Three. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root-cause condition, nine; in the case of object condition, nine … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition, nine. (Abbreviated. Non-predominance Condition:

With respect to predominance, there are nine; with respect to prenascence, nine; with respect to postnascence, nine; with respect to repetition, nine; with respect to kamma, three; with respect to result, nine; with respect to dissociation, nine. (Abbreviated.

in the object-condition (*ārammaṇa*), nine; in the predominance-condition (*adhipati*), nine ... [etc. ... in the decisive-support, the repetition, the kamma, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, and path-conditions, there are three; in the association-condition (*sampayutta*), nine ... [etc. ... in the non-disappearance-condition (*avigata*), nine. (Abbreviated.

With root condition, not-object: four. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object: nine. (Abbreviated.

3.4.6. The Couplets on the Untainted and Tainted Dissociated from the Taints (Āsavavippayutta-sāsavaduka). Question Section (Pañhāvāra) 3.4.6.1.
The Wholesome Category (Kusalapada).
Root condition:

Dependent on a wholesome state that is dissociated from the taints but still subject to taints, there arises a wholesome state dissociated from the taints but still subject to taints, by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state dissociated from the taints and free from taints... [there arises] a state dissociated from the taints... by way of root condition.
An untainted wholesome state arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.

3.4.6.2. Indeterminate Section (Abyākatapada) 3.4.5.2.1–6. The Section on "Dependent on" Etc. (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka)

Conditioned by a root-cause (hetu) dhamma that is dissociated from the taints (āsava), associated with the taints, and indeterminate (abyākata), there arises a dhamma that is dissociated from the taints, associated with the taints, and indeterminate, through the condition of root-cause (hetupaccaya). Conditioned by a root-cause dhamma that is dissociated from the taints, dissociated from the taints, and indeterminate...
[there arises] a dhamma that is dissociated from the taints, dissociated from the taints, and indeterminate.

A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints (*āsava*), untainted (*anāsava*), and indeterminate (*abyākata*), there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints, tainted (*sāsava*), and indeterminate, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints, untainted, and indeterminate, there arise both a state that is dissociated from the taints, tainted, and indeterminate, and a state that is dissociated from the taints, untainted, and indeterminate, by way of root condition.
And indeterminate states arise with root condition.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints but subject to them and indeterminate, as well as a state that is dissociated from the taints and free from them and indeterminate, there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints but subject to them and indeterminate, by way of root condition.

(Abbreviated. In the case of root [condition], there are five; in the case of object, two; in the case of predominance, five ... [and so on] ... in the case of repetition, one; in the case of kamma, five; in the case of result, five ... [and so on] ... in the case of non-disappearance, five. (Abbreviated.)

By way of non-root condition (*nahetupaccaya*): dependent on a state that is not a root, is dissociated from the taints (*āsava*), is subject to the taints, and is indeterminate (*abyākata*), there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints, is subject to the taints, and is indeterminate.

(Abbreviated. Under non-root condition there is one; under non-object condition (*naārammaṇa*) there are three; under non-predominance condition (*naadhipati*) there are two ... pe ... under non-prenascence condition (*napurejāta*) there are four; under non-postnascence condition (*napacchājāta*) ... [and so forth].

In the "not-by-repetition" [condition], there are five; in the "not-by-kamma" and "not-by-resultant" ...pe... in the "not-by-path" [condition], there is one ...pe... in the "not-by-dissociation" [condition], there are two ...pe... in the "not-by-disappearance" [condition], there are three. (Abbreviated.

3.4.6.2.7. Question Section (Pañhāvāra)
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root and Object.

A state that is dissociated from the taints, yet is itself subject to taints and is indeterminate, is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a state that is dissociated from the taints, is subject to taints, and is indeterminate.
A state that is dissociated from the taints, untainted, and indeterminate is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is dissociated from the taints, untainted, and indeterminate.

A state that is dissociated from the taints, untainted, and indeterminate is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is dissociated from the taints, tainted, and indeterminate. A state that is dissociated from the taints, untainted, and indeterminate...
A state dissociated from the taints (āsava), whether it be tainted (sāsava) or indeterminate (abyākata), is a condition for a state dissociated from the taints,
whether it be tainted or indeterminate, by way of the root-condition (hetu-paccaya).

A state dissociated from the taints, which is tainted and indeterminate, is a condition for a state dissociated from the taints, which is tainted and indeterminate, by way of the object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya).
A state that is dissociated from the taints, untainted, and indeterminate is related to a state that is dissociated from the taints, untainted, and indeterminate by way of object-condition.

A state that is dissociated from the taints, untainted, and indeterminate is related to a state that is dissociated from the taints, with taints, and indeterminate by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated.)

in kamma-condition, four; in result-condition, four; in nutriment-condition, four … pe … in association-condition, two.
With dissociation, three; ... [and so on] ... with non-disappearance, seven. (Abbreviated.

It is a condition by way of object-condition … by way of conascence-condition … by way of decisive-support-condition … by way of pre-nascence-condition … by way of post-nascence-condition … by way of nutriment-condition … by way of faculty-condition. (Abbreviated.)
Seven by way of not-root; seven by way of not-object. (Abbreviated.
